newsitem.title: UK: Barratt says sales growth continuing.
newsitem.headline: Barratt says sales growth continuing.

text.p: UK housebuilder Barratt Developments Plc saw year profits bounce 10 percent higher to 52.1 million stg and reported that revenue continues to grow in the current financial year.
Sir Lawrie Barratt, chairman welcomed the rise in year profits to June 30 despite "difficult conditions."
He added: "In our current financial year, we have experienced an upturn in most parts of the country and our sales revenue shows continued growth."
Barratt said the results for the financial year vindicated its policy of organic growth, adding that its future position did not hinge on an overall increase in the UK housing market.
The chairman also said that "house prices over the next few years will not escalate beyond earnings growth".
"We do not seek, nor do we expect, any improvement in the very substantial UK housing market," he added.
The results showed turnover rising 10 percent to 634 million stg, with 7,025 housing completions in the UK, a six percent rise. The average sale price was 83,800 stg, also up six percent.
Group chief executive Frank Eaton said in a divisional summary that the UK housing market had enjoyed a gradual return of confidence in the south of England.
He said the group was well placed to exploit this factor because of new housing divisions set up principally in this area.

In his summary of land activities, he accused the government of failing in its planning policy, with authorities missing applicaiton targets 90 percent of the time. This has resulted in a shortage of development land, he said, putting pressure on land prices and the government's inflation target.
